title: No inventory of providers, routes, SDKs, OAuth apps, tokens, webhooks, syncs, indexes, Relay tools or external actions — and nothing stops a new one appearing unrecorded
why_open: Confirmed absent on disk today: `ls tools/work-graph-inventory.mjs docs/architecture/work-graph-inventory.md` -> both 'No such file or directory'. `ls docs/architecture` has CURRENT-STATE-INVENTORY.md, entry-points.md, subsystem-paths.md, aws-inventory.json and repository-map.json, none of which enumerate the WRK surface. `ls tests/architecture` (27 files) and `ls tests/security` (32 files) contain no work-graph inventory ratchet. The honest inventory is mostly zeros and that is exactly what makes it worth committing and ratcheting: there are no OAuth apps, no webhook receivers and no external actions; there is exactly ONE outbound vendor host (apps/web/src/lib/ai.ts:123 `fetch("https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages")`, model-id-allowlisted at ai.ts:61-98 and partition-checked by `aiConfigured()` at ai.ts:38); the Relay tool surface is whatever the module catalog declares and apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.ts:441 `authorizeRelayTools` collects; the one retrieval index is apps/web/src/lib/search-data.ts:25 `loadSearchCorpus`; the scheduled jobs are exactly three — `ls apps/web/src/app/api/jobs` -> outbox, reminders, slo. Without a committed inventory plus a ratchet, WRK-000-002 (classify each with evidence — the vocabulary for which ALREADY EXISTS unused in packages/provisioning/src/connector-capability.ts:60-74) has no input, and the first connector merged is invisible to it. The repo already proves the pattern: tools/entry-point-inventory.mjs generates docs/architecture/entry-points.md and tests/security/entry-points.test.mjs fails when the committed copy is stale.
smallest_real_change: Copy the shape of tools/entry-point-inventory.mjs exactly (it already supports `--check`). New tools/work-graph-inventory.mjs `collect()` walks the tree and returns, from CODE not prose: every tool registration declared by the module catalog with its `requiredPermission`/`readOnly`/`reauthorizesPerCall`; every outbound network host reachable from apps/web/src (parse `fetch(`/`new URL(` literal targets — today that is one host, ai.ts:123); every route under apps/web/src/app/api; every directory under apps/web/src/app/api/jobs; every env var NAME that denotes a provider credential (NAME ONLY — never read a value, and assert that in the tool's own header); and an explicit empty-by-construction list for OAuth apps, webhook receivers and external actions. Reuse the EXISTING status vocabulary — import `ConnectorCapabilityStatus` from packages/provisioning/src/connector-capability.ts:60 rather than inventing a second one, so WRK-000-002 has a column to fill instead of a document to reconcile. New tests/architecture/work-graph-inventory.test.mjs asserts three things, mirroring tests/security/entry-points.test.mjs: (a) `node tools/work-graph-inventory.mjs --check` reports up to date; (b) every tool registration collected from the module catalog appears in the committed doc; (c) every outbound host found under apps/web/src appears in the doc's outbound table. MUTATION PROOF: add a throwaway tool registration to the module catalog, run the test WITHOUT regenerating, confirm (a) and (b) both red; regenerate, confirm green; delete it and regenerate. Separately add `fetch('https://example.invalid')` inside apps/web/src/lib/ai.ts, confirm (c) reds, remove it. Run `node --test tests/architecture/work-graph-inventory.test.mjs` and `npm run test:platform`. Append the row to docs/implementation/universal-work-graph-execution-ledger.md:22 with the command and its exit code.

title: Only 5 of the 9 required connect paths exist — scope upgrade, resource selection, reauth, provider-sign-up, request-integration and alternative-source have no representation at all
why_open: The requirement names nine paths: user connect, scope upgrade, resource selection, reauth, ask-admin, provider-sign-up, request-integration, alternative-source, unavailable. `ConnectionOutcome` (apps/web/src/lib/connections/capability-resolution.ts:25-35) has exactly five members — CONNECTED, NEEDS_USER_CONNECT, NEEDS_ADMIN, NOT_CERTIFIED, UNAVAILABLE — and the action union at :66 has four kinds: connect | ask-admin | disconnect | none. So user-connect, ask-admin and unavailable are covered; the other six are not expressible, and `resolveCapability` (:73-123) has no branch that could produce them. `grep -rn 'reauth|scopeUpgrade|resourceSelection|requestIntegration|alternativeSource|provider-sign-up' apps/web/src` returns only `reauthorizesPerCall` (a different concept — per-call re-authorization of a Relay tool, relay-tools.ts:38) and NextAuth session-refresh test names. This is not a paper module: `resolveCapability` has two real production callers — apps/web/src/app/(app)/settings/page.tsx:96 maps it over `declaredConnections` (:50-88, three real capabilities read from `aiConfigured()`/`storageConfigured()`), and apps/web/src/components/connections/MissingConnectionCard.tsx:44 calls it to decide the single control a card offers. The file's own header (:13-22) is honest that no provider `Connection` record exists, which is exactly why the buildable half is the DECISION vocabulary: three of the six missing paths need no provider at all. `calendar.feed` is declared `configured: true` unconditionally at settings/page.tsx:79 with the comment 'there is nothing to provision' — that is the resource-selection path (WHICH calendars) collapsed to a boolean, and the ICS feed is per-user and real.
smallest_real_change: Extend `ConnectionOutcome` and the action union in capability-resolution.ts with the paths that are decidable from state this deployment genuinely has, and REFUSE to add the ones that would be canned. Add: NEEDS_SCOPE_UPGRADE (state gains `grantedScopes`/`requiredScopes`; outcome fires when granted is a strict subset — the same subset test packages/platform-config's `providerActivation` already applies to the vendor's scopes, cited so there is one rule); NEEDS_RESOURCE_SELECTION (state gains `selectableResources: {selected:number; available:number} | null`; fires when available>0 and selected===0 — connected but pointed at nothing, which today renders as CONNECTED); NEEDS_REAUTH (state gains `credentialExpiresAt: string | null`; fires when expired — reuse `connectionHealth` from @tenure/provisioning exactly as apps/web/src/lib/auth-connections.ts:117 does, do NOT write a second expiry rule); and for NOT_CERTIFIED add `alternative` to the resolution so 'nothing to connect' names what still works instead of being a dead end (the prose already exists in settings/page.tsx:64 'Retrieval and search keep working without it' — move it from a hand-written string into the resolution). Do NOT add provider-sign-up or request-integration outcomes: with zero certified third-party providers they would have no producer, and a dead outcome is worse than an honest gap — state that refusal in the header and in the ledger row. MAKE THE NEW `CapabilityState` FIELDS REQUIRED, not optional, so `tsc` names every construction site; the sites are exactly the three literals in settings/page.tsx:53-86 plus the fixtures in capability-resolution.test.ts and MissingConnectionCard's callers — grep `CapabilityState` before and after and name each. Populate them from real values: `credentialExpiresAt` from the same env-backed reference auth-connections.ts:72 reads, `selectableResources` for `calendar.feed` from the count of calendars the viewer can subscribe to. MUTATION PROOF (mutate the PRODUCER): in settings/page.tsx set `calendar.feed`'s selected count to a non-zero constant and confirm the page-level test reds because the card stops asking for resource selection; separately delete the subset comparison in resolveCapability and confirm the scope-upgrade case reds. Restore both. Run `npm run test --workspace apps/web -- --ci connections` and `npx playwright test apps/web/e2e` for the settings flow.

title: Authorization is not auditable on the one surface that exposes tenant rows to a model — the AI chat route makes a full permission decision per request and persists none of it
why_open: The gate requires authorization be 'least-privilege, provider-compliant, revocable, and AUDITABLE'. The first three are genuinely built (apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.ts:441 `authorizeRelayTools` runs three gates, :562 `invokeRelayTool` is the single door, the world is rebuilt per call so a revoked seat stops answering). The fourth does not exist. `grep -n 'db\.|recordAuditEvent|create(' apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts` returns ZERO hits across all 448 lines: the route computes `tools` (:236), runs `invokeRelayTool` (:245), assembles a rich decision object carrying `policyRevision` per offered tool, `riskClass`, and each refusal's `disclosure`/`safeReason`/`remedy` (:407-439) — and then returns it in the HTTP response and forgets it. The route's own comment at :415-419 says a decision that cannot name the policy it was taken under 'is not explainable six months later' — and nothing writes that name anywhere durable, so it is explainable only to whoever was holding the browser tab. Every other decision surface in the tree does persist: `grep -rln recordAuditEvent apps/web/src` -> admin/payments/actions.ts, approvals/actions.ts, orgs/[slug]/finance/actions.ts, lib/admin/guard.ts, lib/provisioning/reconcile.ts, lib/tenancy/context.ts. The model-exposure path — the one that hands other people's message bodies, document descriptions and event details to a third-party vendor — is the only one that does not. There is also no record of a REFUSAL, so 'the assistant was not allowed to' leaves no trace at all.
smallest_real_change: Write the relay authorization decision to the audit chain through `recordAuditEvent` from @/lib/audit-record — NOT `db.auditEvent.create`, which is ratcheted at 32 in tests/security/audit-writes.test.mjs and may only fall. One event per request, inside the tenant scope the route already opens, carrying: action `Relay.ToolInvoked` or `Relay.ToolRefused`, resourceType `RelayTool`, resourceId = the resolved `toolKey`, outcome ALLOW/DENY, and metadata { riskClass, policyRevision, configRevision, surfaceAllow, refusalReason, sourceCount } — the values the route ALREADY computes at :407-439, so this is a write of facts that exist rather than new computation. Never the question text, never a source body: the metadata is the decision, not the content, and the header must say so. Emit for refusals too — a denial nobody can find is the failure this gate is about. The jest mock of @/lib/db in the route's existing tests must implement BOTH forms of `$transaction` (array AND callback) because `recordAuditEvent` appends the chain through the callback form, and the implementation must be re-stated inside `beforeEach` since `jest.clearAllMocks()` wipes implementations. TEST in apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/relay-prompt-safety.test.ts: drive the real route with a proposal that is offered and assert an ALLOW row was appended naming the toolKey and a non-null policyRevision; drive one that is refused (a proposal naming `tenantId`, which relay-tools.ts refuses outright) and assert a DENY row with the refusal reason and NO source text in metadata. MUTATION PROOF (mutate the PRODUCER, not the helper): delete the `recordAuditEvent` call from route.ts and confirm both tests red; separately change the route to pass a hardcoded `policyRevision: 'r1'` instead of the value read off `tools.offered[].decision.policyRevision` and confirm the ALLOW test reds — that second mutation is the one that catches the frozen-constant failure mode. Restore, confirm green. Run `npm run test --workspace apps/web -- --ci ai/chat` and `npm run test:isolation`, since the route is a live request path.

title: No Connection Credential Broker — a long-lived reusable provider secret is read straight out of process.env at the vendor call site, with no reference indirection, no expiry and no single door
why_open: `grep -rni 'credential broker|CredentialBroker|token vault|tokenVault' apps/web/src packages` returns nothing outside other ledgers' prose (docs/implementation/integration-ecosystem-execution-ledger.md:86). The real code reads the raw secret at the moment of use: apps/web/src/lib/ai.ts:127 `"x-api-key": process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY!` inside the `fetch` to api.anthropic.com, and apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:169 `clientSecret: process.env.OKTA_CLIENT_SECRET!`. Both are long-lived, reusable, and have no expiry the code can see. The contrast that makes this a real defect rather than a missing feature is one file away: apps/web/src/lib/auth-connections.ts:65-74 already models a credential as a REFERENCE — `{ purpose, ref, expiresAt, lastRotatedAt }` with the comment 'The registry requires a reference rather than a value... The value never appears here' — and `oktaIsUsable` (:113-121) refuses a connection whose credential has expired via `connectionHealth`. That machinery is applied to the Okta connection's DESCRIPTION and bypassed entirely by the code that actually uses the secret at auth.ts:169; the vendor key gets none of it at all. So the platform has a working expiry/rotation vocabulary and no chokepoint that forces anything through it, and nothing prevents the next `process.env.SOMETHING_API_KEY` appearing at a fourth call site.
smallest_real_change: New apps/web/src/lib/connections/credential-broker.ts exporting `borrowProviderCredential(purpose)` -> `{ ok: true; use<T>(fn: (secret: string) => Promise<T>): Promise<T> } | { ok: false; reason: 'not-configured' | 'expired' | 'unreferenced' }`. Three properties make it a broker rather than a getter and each is testable: (1) it returns a CAPABILITY, not the value — the secret is passed to a callback and never returned, so no caller can hold it past the call and no log line can interpolate it; (2) it resolves through the SAME `IdentityConnection` credential-reference record auth-connections.ts:65-74 already builds and refuses an expired one by calling `connectionHealth` from @tenure/provisioning — do not write a second expiry rule; (3) it is the only door. Rewire the two real callers: ai.ts:123-131 wraps the `fetch` in `borrowProviderCredential('anthropic-api-key').use(secret => fetch(..., {headers:{'x-api-key': secret}}))` and returns null on a refusal exactly as it already does when unconfigured (the route degrades to sources-only, which is behaviour that already exists at ai.ts:38); auth.ts:168-170 takes the Okta client secret the same way, and `oktaIsUsable` becomes the broker's refusal rather than a second check beside it. Add tests/security/provider-secrets-go-through-the-broker.test.mjs modelled on tests/security/no-tokens-in-browser-storage.test.mjs: walk apps/web/src and fail on any `process.env.<NAME>` where NAME matches /_(API_KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD)$/ outside credential-broker.ts and the env-schema module — that is the ratchet that makes the door real for code not yet written. Allow-list DEV_LOGIN_PASSPHRASE explicitly with a dated comment (auth.ts:188 — it is compared, not sent to a provider) rather than silently. Confirm the test NEVER reads or prints a value; it matches names only. MUTATION PROOF (producer): revert ai.ts to `process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY!` at the fetch and confirm the architecture test reds naming that line; separately make the broker return the secret string instead of a `use()` capability and confirm the unit test asserting the value never escapes reds. Restore both. Run `node --test tests/security/provider-secrets-go-through-the-broker.test.mjs`, `npm run test --workspace apps/web -- --ci ai`, `npm run test:platform`.

title: Zero cost allocation for model use and provider calls — aiComplete discards the vendor's own token usage, so no tenant is ever charged and no budget can be enforced
why_open: The requirement names tokens, provider calls, workers, queues, payloads, parsing, indexing, model use, backfill and retained state. The single outbound vendor call meters NONE of it: apps/web/src/lib/ai.ts:135 parses the response as `(await res.json()) as { content?: { type: string; text?: string }[] }` — the cast literally excludes `usage`, which is the field the Anthropic messages API returns input_tokens/output_tokens in, so the numbers arrive on the wire and are dropped on the floor. `grep -n 'usage|input_tokens|output_tokens' apps/web/src/lib/ai.ts` returns nothing; the only token reference in the file is `max_tokens: maxTokens` (:112), a CAP, which is the opposite of a measurement. There is no counter of provider calls either, and `aiComplete` has four call sites (chat/route.ts:351 plus ai.ts:172, :191, :217) all of which return prose without a cost. No budget exists anywhere: nothing refuses a call because a tenant has spent its allowance. The retained-state half already has a real answer in packages/provisioning/src/residual-reconciliation.ts (a per-lifecycle-state resource claim reconciled against observation), which is the model to follow and also the proof this is a gap and not a decision — that file's header explicitly says 'Cost ALLOCATION — dollars, budgets, tags — lives in @tenure/finops. This package does not import it', and nothing in apps/web imports it either.
smallest_real_change: Two halves. (1) MEASURE: widen the response cast in apps/web/src/lib/ai.ts:135 to read `usage: { input_tokens: number; output_tokens: number }` and return it. `aiComplete` currently returns `string | null` and has FOUR call sites (chat/route.ts:351, ai.ts:172, :191, :217) — grep `aiComplete` and fix all four in the same change; prefer an added `onUsage` callback parameter over widening the return type precisely because a widened return is silently ignorable by a caller that does not destructure it, whereas an unimplemented required callback is a `tsc` error. (2) ALLOCATE: new apps/web/src/lib/metering/model-usage.ts `recordModelUsage({ institutionId, model, inputTokens, outputTokens, at })` that writes a per-tenant meter row, and `budgetVerdict(institutionId, at)` that compares the period total against a cap read from the tenant's PUBLISHED CONFIGURATION (apps/web/src/lib/config/server.ts — the same place the chat route already reads `configRevision` from), never from NODE_ENV and never a constant. `aiComplete`'s production caller in chat/route.ts:351 calls `budgetVerdict` BEFORE the vendor call and degrades to the existing sources-only answer when over budget — that path already exists for the unconfigured case, so the refusal is a real behaviour and not a new error surface. Persisting the meter needs a table; that means apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma plus a migration — STATE THAT EXPLICITLY in the result, because a second run is in this tree. If the schema is contended, land the meter against the EXISTING `OutboxEvent`-style pattern is NOT acceptable (wrong semantics) — instead land part (1) plus an in-request accumulator with the itest proving the numbers are real, and return FAIL on the persistence half naming schema.prisma. Do NOT edit packages/finops — it is owned by the concurrent STUDIO run; import from it read-only if pricing is needed, or keep tokens as tokens and leave dollars to a later item. TEST: unit-test `budgetVerdict` boundary (at cap = allowed, one over = refused). MUTATION PROOF (producer): in ai.ts return a hardcoded `{input_tokens: 0, output_tokens: 0}` instead of the parsed usage and confirm the itest reds because the meter total stops moving with the fixture's response; separately delete the `budgetVerdict` call from route.ts:351 and confirm the route test reds because an over-budget tenant gets prose. Restore both. Run `npm run test --workspace apps/web -- --ci ai` and `npm run test:isolation`.

title: No coverage reconciliation between what was audited and what was published — a transition that forgets its outbox event is invisible, and no exception has an owner
why_open: The dispatcher itself is now real and good (apps/web/src/app/api/jobs/outbox/route.ts:90 calls `dispatchOnce`, :97 calls `gaps`, and prisma-ports.ts:184-192 reclaims expired leases). What does not exist is reconciliation of COVERAGE: whether an event that should have been emitted was. The producer writes the audit row and the outbox row side by side inside one transaction — apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/actions.ts:278 `tx.auditEvent.create({ action: target ? 'Approval.Submitted' : 'Approval.DraftCreated' })` then :296 `tx.outboxEvent.create` guarded by `if (target)`, with a deliberate asymmetry explained at :289-294 (a draft audits but must NOT emit). That asymmetry is the whole reason a reconciliation is needed and is not tautological: the rule 'Approval.Submitted MUST have a matching OutboxEvent, Approval.DraftCreated MUST NOT' lives only in that `if`, and the next writer who adds a transition has nothing that notices when they forget. The same pattern repeats at :443/:598 and :894/:914. Today `gaps` (outbox.ts, surfaced at route.ts:118-120) counts only `overdue` and `dead` — rows that EXIST and have not moved. A row that was never written counts as zero overdue, which reads as healthy. And nothing names an owner: the job response returns `dead: <number>` with no per-institution owner, so a dead-lettered event belongs to nobody. `grep -rn 'orphan|exception owner' apps/web/src` returns nothing on this subject.
smallest_real_change: New apps/web/src/lib/outbox/coverage.ts declaring the emission contract as DATA — `EMISSION_RULES: { auditAction, mustEmit: boolean, eventType, owner }[]` covering the three real pairs in approvals/actions.ts (Approval.Submitted -> ApprovalRequested required; Approval.DraftCreated -> none; and the pairs at :443/:598 and :894/:914) — plus `reconcileCoverage(ports, { since, now })` which, inside the institution's own tenant scope, joins AuditEvent to OutboxEvent on `resourceId = correlationId` and returns two asymmetric findings, exactly as packages/provisioning/src/residual-reconciliation.ts does for cost: `missing` (audited, required, no event — a change nothing downstream learned about) and `unexpected` (an event with no audited cause). Every finding carries `owner` from the rule, so an exception belongs to a named role rather than to a count. Call it from the EXISTING job route inside the same `forEachInstitution` pass at route.ts:87-100 — that is the production caller, no new endpoint — and add `uncovered`/`unexpected` totals to the response beside `overdue`/`dead`. Keep the route's existing discipline: counts and owners only, NEVER a payload (route.ts:27-30 says why). TEST apps/web/src/lib/outbox/coverage.itest.ts against real Postgres (`docker ps` shows it up): seed one institution, submit an approval through the real action so BOTH rows are written by the production path, assert zero findings; then insert an `Approval.Submitted` AuditEvent with no OutboxEvent and assert one `missing` finding naming the owner; then create a DRAFT and assert it produces NO finding, which is the asymmetry test. MUTATION PROOF (mutate the PRODUCER, not the helper): comment out the `tx.outboxEvent.create` at approvals/actions.ts:296 and confirm the itest reds with a `missing` finding — restore immediately; separately flip that rule's `mustEmit` to false and confirm the same test reds. Run `npm run test --workspace apps/web -- --ci outbox` and `npm run test:isolation` with DATABASE_URL set. NOTE for the implementer: approvals/actions.ts is only MUTATED temporarily here, never left changed — the production change is confined to lib/outbox and the job route.

title: The signed release binds modules, configuration and schema — and nothing about connectors: no app registrations, scopes, tools, provider reviews, certification evidence, runbooks or rollback plan are inside the checksum
why_open: `ReleaseContent` (packages/releases/src/release.ts:184-193) is exactly nine fields: tenantId, blueprintId/Version, topologyId/Version, modules, configurationChecksum, policyIds, schemaVersion. `contentOf` (:195-222) hashes those and only those, and `signRelease` (:249-264) HMACs the same bytes — the file's own comment at :223 says 'The exact bytes both the checksum and the signature are taken over'. So a release can be signed and approved while the connector surface underneath it changes freely: PROVIDER_PACKS (packages/provisioning/src/provider-packs.ts:126-378, 24 providers including all ten this domain's WRK-100-001 names), the `providerReview` records the AI route's activation gate reads (apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:278-300), the `evidenceRefs` that `capabilityProblems` demands for an AVAILABLE claim (packages/provisioning/src/connector-capability.ts:100, :137), and every tool registration `authorizeRelayTools` will offer — none of them are covered. Two releases that pin identical modules but ship a different scope set or a withdrawn provider review hash IDENTICALLY today, which is the precise defect the header at release.ts:62-70 already articulates for module lifecycle and then fixed only for lifecycle. Rollback is a state transition (`rollbackTo`, :444) with no bound plan. There is exactly ONE production producer — packages/platform-config/src/build-system.ts:278 `createRelease(releaseInput)` — so the construction-site blast radius is one file plus apps/web/src/lib/system/reference-systems.test.ts:261.
smallest_real_change: Add ONE field to `ReleaseContent` and `SystemRelease`: `connectorBindingChecksum: string` — a sha256 over the sorted, stable-stringified connector surface (each `ConnectorCapability` tuple from packages/provisioning/src/connector-capability.ts:104 `capabilityKey`, its status, its scope set, its `evidenceRefs`, and each pack's provider-review state and runbook/rollback ref). A CHECKSUM rather than the whole surface inlined, for the same reason `configurationChecksum` is already a checksum at release.ts:113: the release stays a small citable artifact and the binding is still total, because any change to any of those bytes changes the release's own checksum and therefore invalidates its signature. Make it REQUIRED, not optional — an optional field a producer forgets to set is invisible to `tsc` and would compile while binding nothing, which is the exact failure mode this survey is told to avoid. Then fix every construction site in the same change and NAME THEM: packages/platform-config/src/build-system.ts:278 (the only production producer — it already has the module catalog in hand, so it computes the checksum from the same source `providerActivation` reads), packages/releases/src/releases.test.ts fixtures, apps/web/src/lib/system/reference-systems.test.ts:261, apps/web/src/lib/system/build-system.test.ts. BEFORE editing, grep `SystemRelease`/`ReleaseInput`/`createRelease` across apps/ and packages/ and CONFIRM apps/system-studio only READS a release (apps/system-studio/src/lib/deliver.ts mirrors `transition`) and never constructs one — if it constructs one, STOP and return FAIL naming apps/system-studio, which the concurrent STUDIO run owns and this run must not touch. Add `diffReleases` (:506) coverage so an approver sees the connector surface moved. MUTATION PROOF (producer): in build-system.ts:278 pass a constant `'sha256:0'` for the new field and confirm the test asserting two releases with different provider-review states hash differently reds — that mutation is on the PRODUCER and catches the frozen-constant failure; separately drop the field out of `contentOf` and confirm the same test reds because the signature stops covering it. Restore both. Run `npm run test --workspace packages/releases`, `npm run test --workspace apps/web -- --ci system`, `npm run type-check` across the monorepo.

title: Orphan recovery is absent and its absence FAILS OPEN — deleting a Role silently converts every seat-private memory card, including CREDENTIAL cards, into an org-wide readable one
why_open: The requirement is personal-versus-organization ownership, owner succession, and orphan recovery. Succession exists for the institution Director role only (apps/web/src/app/(app)/admin/actions.ts:616-703 opens a RoleTransfer, :704+ accepts it in one transaction). Nothing exists for the work-graph objects those seats own, and the gap is not merely a missing feature — it is a silent privacy widening. `MemoryRecord.roleId` is `String?` with `role Role? @relation(fields: [roleId], references: [id])` (apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma:785-786) and NO `onDelete`, so Prisma's default for an optional relation is SetNull. `canSeeMemoryCard` (apps/web/src/lib/memory.ts:16) reads `if (!card.roleId) return true` — a null roleId means 'org-wide: anyone who can view the org' (:5). Therefore deleting a Role converts every card scoped to that seat into an org-wide card, and `MemoryRecordType` includes `CREDENTIAL // Login / access info` (schema.prisma:772) and `BUDGET`/`VENDOR`. The accept-transfer transaction (admin/actions.ts:704-770) touches roleTransfer, institutionMembership and auditEvent and NOTHING else — `grep -n 'memoryRecord' ` over that block returns nothing — so even a successful succession does not carry the seat's knowledge across, despite the notification text at :275 promising 'the seat's knowledge stays for your successor'. `Document.createdById` (schema.prisma:757) and `MemoryRecord.authorId` (:790) are bare `String?` with no relation at all, so nothing even guarantees the named owner exists. `grep -rn 'orphan' apps/web/src` returns no hits on this subject: there is no query that finds an ownerless object and no path that recovers one.
smallest_real_change: Close the fail-open first, because it is a live disclosure and needs no schema change: in apps/web/src/lib/memory.ts, stop inferring org-wide from a null roleId. A card must say what it is rather than have it derived from the absence of a pointer. Smallest honest version without touching the schema: `canSeeMemoryCard` takes the card's `roleId` AND a new explicit `scope: 'ORG' | 'SEAT'`, and a SEAT card whose roleId is null is ORPHANED — visible to OSE and the org's ACTIVE president only (the two roles memory.ts already trusts at :17 and :23-26), never to the whole org.
